subject: Security review: Offline bundle signing + upgrade/rollback audit logging (Redwood Private)
related_links: Linear: ENG-2324 (Security review: secrets handling during backup, bundle signing keys, audit logging requirements for upgrade actions)
Jira: INT-331 (Signing key rotation process + document verification failures)

body:
From: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 14, 2025 at 9:12 AM
Subject: Security review: Offline bundle signing + upgrade/rollback audit logging (Redwood Private)

Connor,

As part of the security sign-off for “Private upgrade + rollback mechanism” (including air-gapped/on-prem), I need written answers + evidence on:

1) Bundle signing
- What artifacts are signed (bundle tarball, manifest, individual images/helm charts)?
- What signature format are we using and what’s the verification UX in the installer (hard fail vs warn, flags)?
- What prevents a malicious operator from bypassing verification?

2) Key custody / access control
- Where do signing keys live (KMS/HSM/Vault)? Can keys be exported?
- Who has access (humans and CI roles)? How is access reviewed?
- Rotation/revocation plan (including what happens to older bundles, and how customers get updated trust roots if needed)

3) Provenance + auditability
- What provenance metadata do we generate (build pipeline, git SHA, builder identity)?
- What audit log events do we emit for upgrade/rollback actions (who/when/what/where), and how do they flow in VPC vs on-prem?

Please reply with:
- short written answers inline
- pointers to any implementation docs and the PRs
- sample audit event payload(s)

Target: EOW so we can unblock beta enablement.

Thanks,
Aisha

—
Dr. Aisha Rahman
Security Executive Sponsor
Redwood Inference



From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 14, 2025 at 12:47 PM
Subject: Re: Security review: Offline bundle signing + upgrade/rollback audit logging (Redwood Private)

Aisha — replying inline below. Vivek FYI since this impacts GA gates.

> 1) Bundle signing
> - What artifacts are signed (bundle tarball, manifest, individual images/helm charts)?

For v1:
- We sign the *bundle manifest* (JSON) which includes a digest list for:
  - installer binary
  - helm chart packages (.tgz)
  - image digests referenced by the charts (we require digest-pinned images)
  - any migrations/jobs images
- The bundle tarball is also checksummed (sha256) but our integrity anchor is the signed manifest + digest verification during import.

We are not currently signing each image with a separate signature in customer registries; instead we verify the digest set declared in the signed manifest. (We can expand to per-image signatures later if required.)

> - What signature format are we using and what’s the verification UX in the installer (hard fail vs warn, flags)?

- Signature format: cosign signature over the manifest payload.
- Installer behavior (air-gapped import path):
  - Default: hard fail if signature verification fails OR if any artifact digest mismatches.
  - There is no “--insecure” bypass flag on the offline import subcommand.
  - Error message includes failure reason (invalid signature / unknown key id / digest mismatch / manifest parse).

> - What prevents a malicious operator from bypassing verification?

- Offline import verifies before we unpack into the local bundle cache directory used by subsequent upgrade steps.
- Upgrade command only accepts bundles from the local cache that have a verified manifest record.
- We do have non-interactive flags for automation (e.g. --yes) but they don’t disable verification.

> 2) Key custody / access control
> - Where do signing keys live (KMS/HSM/Vault)? Can keys be exported?

Current plan:
- Signing key is in AWS KMS (hardware-backed) for Redwood-managed builds.
- Key material is non-exportable.
- CI uses an OIDC-bound role to request signing operations; no developer laptops.

> - Who has access (humans and CI roles)? How is access reviewed?

- Only release CI role can invoke kms:Sign.
- Break-glass access is limited to Release Eng on-call and requires Security approval (tracked in our access review process). We can enumerate the IAM principals in the evidence pack.

> - Rotation/revocation plan

- Rotation: quarterly target. We’ll keep multiple public keys in the installer trust store (allowlist) to validate older bundles for a defined window.
- Revocation: if compromise suspected, we ship a new installer with the revoked key removed; for customers who cannot immediately upgrade installer, we can provide an out-of-band “updated trust store” file signed by a still-trusted key.

> 3) Provenance + auditability

- Manifest includes git SHAs for installer + chart repo commits, build timestamp, CI run id, and artifact digests.
- Upgrade/rollback audit events:
  - Control plane emits audit entries for upgrade.start, upgrade.complete (success/failure), rollback.triggered, rollback.complete.
  - Includes actor (RBAC principal / API key id), target version, previous version, correlation_id.

Linking PRs:
- Offline bundle + verification: redwood-private-installer PR #439
- Audit log events: redwood PR #18477
- Correlation id propagation: redwood PR #18544

I’ll send a separate email tomorrow with a short “evidence pack” PDF + sample audit payload.

-Connor

—
Connor O’Brien
Release Orchestration Lead
Redwood Inference



From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 14, 2025 at 1:26 PM
Subject: Re: Security review: Offline bundle signing + upgrade/rollback audit logging (Redwood Private)

Adding one product note:

We’re treating “no insecure bypass” on offline bundle import as a hard requirement for on-prem. For VPC-connected deployments, we still verify but the artifacts are pulled via our normal release channel (which is already access controlled). The operator-facing docs will explicitly call out the failure mode + next steps when verification fails.

Aisha, if you need us to change the policy (e.g., allow bypass only with a break-glass token), we should decide now since it affects beta timing.

-Vivek

—
Vivek Kulkarni
Product Lead, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference



From: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Jan 15, 2025 at 9:03 AM
Subject: Re: Security review: Offline bundle signing + upgrade/rollback audit logging (Redwood Private)

Thanks both.

Follow-ups before I can sign off:

1) Verification trust root distribution
- Where does the verifier public key live? Embedded in installer binary? Config file? Both?
- For air-gapped customers: how do they validate they have the *correct* installer/trust root initially (i.e., supply chain at “day 0”)?

2) Key rotation mechanics
- Please be explicit on how the trust store updates happen for on-prem customers who intentionally avoid frequent upgrades.
- What is the maximum time we will continue to validate bundles signed with an old key?

3) Audit log coverage
- Do we also log *failed* verification attempts / failed upgrade attempts in a way customers can ship to their SIEM?
- Are audit events emitted from installer-side actions as well, or only from control plane API calls?

If you can include the above in the evidence pack, that’d be ideal.

Aisha



From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Jan 15, 2025 at 5:41 PM
Subject: Re: Security review: Offline bundle signing + upgrade/rollback audit logging (Redwood Private)

Aisha — answers inline + attaching the evidence pack draft.

Attachment: Private_Upgrade_Signing_Evidence_Pack_v1.pdf
Attachment: installer_signature_verification_screenshots.png
Attachment: sample_upgrade_audit_events.json

> 1) Verification trust root distribution
> - Where does the verifier public key live?

- Public key(s) are embedded in the installer at build time AND also written to a local read-only trust store file on install (so we can display/inspect fingerprints via `redwood-private-installer trust list`).
- The installer only trusts keys compiled into it (or updated via a signed trust update file — see below). It does not accept arbitrary local keys without signature.

> - Day 0 supply chain

For day-0:
- We deliver the installer via the same channels as existing on-prem deliverables (Support/PS-assisted distribution for air-gapped accounts).
- The evidence pack includes:
  - SHA256 checksums of installer binaries
  - the signing public key fingerprint(s)
  - instructions for customers to validate checksum out-of-band (e.g. published in the customer portal + provided via Support)

We don’t currently have a public transparency log for these air-gapped releases; our control is checksum + key fingerprint verification. (Open to future improvement.)

> 2) Key rotation mechanics

- Trust updates: for customers who avoid frequent upgrades, we can provide a “trust store update” file (JSON) that contains an updated allowlist of public keys and is itself signed by a currently-trusted key.
- Planned validation window for old keys: 180 days by default (configurable by policy; we can shorten if Security requires).

> 3) Audit log coverage

- Failed verification attempts:
  - Installer writes a structured local log event (`bundle.verify.failed`) including bundle identifier, reason, and correlation id.
  - On on-prem, it is written to the installer logs (and included in the diagnostics bundle). It is not automatically shipped unless the customer forwards logs.

- Failed upgrade attempts:
  - Control plane emits `private_upgrade.failed` with step_id/correlation_id and error category.

- Installer vs control plane audit:
  - “Authoritative” audit events come from the control plane when an upgrade/rollback is initiated (API call) and when state transitions occur.
  - Installer-side actions are logged locally with the same correlation id; for VPC deployments, customers can also forward installer logs to their SIEM if they run the installer in their automation environment.

Evidence pack highlights:
- KMS key policy + non-exportability statement
- CI role permissions excerpt
- Screenshot of installer hard-failing verification
- Sample audit events (JSON)

Let me know what else you want tightened.

-Connor



From: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jan 16, 2025 at 10:18 AM
Subject: Re: Security review: Offline bundle signing + upgrade/rollback audit logging (Redwood Private)

Reviewed — this is close.

Two required changes before sign-off:

1) Key validation window
- 180 days is longer than I’m comfortable with for a signing key allowlist in an air-gapped distribution model. Please propose a policy with:
  - default window (suggest 90 days)
  - explicit exception process for customers who need longer windows

2) Audit event completeness
- Ensure audit events include: actor type (human SSO vs service account/API key), source IP (where available), and deployment identifier/cluster id.
- For on-prem: we need a clear statement in docs that customers must forward installer logs if they want visibility into failed verification attempts. Otherwise, it will be missed.

If you confirm these will land in the next iteration, I’m good to sign off for beta.

Aisha



From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jan 16, 2025 at 4:48 PM
Subject: Re: Security review: Offline bundle signing + upgrade/rollback audit logging (Redwood Private)

Confirmed.

1) Validation window
- We’ll change default allowlist validation window to 90 days.
- Exception: documented Support/Security approval path for customers requiring extended windows (tracked as INT-331 follow-up).

2) Audit event fields
- We’ll add actor_type + source_ip (best-effort) + private_deployment_id to the audit events emitted by control plane.
- Docs: Kira is updating on-prem guidance to explicitly call out installer log forwarding for verification failures.

I’ll reply again once the PRs are merged and the evidence pack is updated.

-Connor
